_: NEW-78: what the speech worker does with the microphone while push to talk is held, before any client draws it. Only the voice device listens, so ONE implementation replays this (apps/desktop/crates/voice/src/listen.rs); the clients ×4 draw the `level` events (VoiceWave, NEW-54 b2) and never recompute them. Audio is mono 16 kHz in frames of 512 samples (32 ms, Silero's frame): every frame yields one `level` event (`level` + 8 `bands`, each 0..1, rounded to 3 decimals). A frame's level = its RMS in dBFS mapped linearly from floorDb (0) to ceilingDb (1), clamped; a band's level = the same mapping of the RMS of its share of a Hann-windowed spectrum (bandEdgesHz, log-spaced). The drawn value moves towards the measured one by `attack` per frame when rising and by `release` when falling. Speech = Silero probabilities per frame: a segment opens at a frame >= threshold, a run of frames below negThreshold starts the silence (frames between the two thresholds keep the segment open), minSilenceMs of silence closes it, a segment with less than minSpeechMs of speech is dropped, padMs of audio is kept on both sides (never reaching back into the previous segment), and a segment is cut at maxSegmentMs. Releasing the key closes the open segment where the speech ended. Every closed segment is transcribed at once (Parakeet), so release waits only for the last; on a GPU the open segment is re-transcribed every partialEveryMs for `partial` (never on the CPU). Transcripts are normalised (whitespace collapsed, no space before . , ! ? ; : % ), nothing without a letter or digit) and the segments joined with one space: empty = `empty`, else `heard`.

wake._: #NEW-56 (voice plan V7, approved 2026-10-27): the wake word, with NO wake-word model. While it is on (the voice device, an agent picked, Wake word on, the tray's Mute off) the speech worker keeps the microphone open and Silero scoring it (the segment rules above); in silence that is all it does. The start of every speech segment is transcribed ONCE by the resident Parakeet, a window sized to the phrase (`window`: windowBaseMs + windowPerLetterMs × the phrase's letters, clamped to windowMinMs … windowMaxMs; `Hey Studio` = 9 letters = 1500 ms; owner decision 2026-10-27: a 2 s window cost 29 % of a CPU core under continuous talk): as soon as the open segment is that long, or when a shorter segment closes (`checks`: [start, end) in frames, padding included, one per segment; a dropped segment is never checked; a segment cut at maxSegmentMs is a new segment). MATCH (`match`): the transcript's `words` are its runs of letters and digits, lowercased, the accents Parakeet writes folded to ASCII (ä→a, ö→o, ü→u, ß→ss, é→e …), an apostrophe joining (What's = whats), anything else separating. The phrase (Settings → Voice `wakePhrase`, empty = `Hey {agent}`) must OPEN the segment: its letters with the spaces dropped are compared (Levenshtein) with the transcript's first 1 … n+2 words joined (n = the phrase's words), the closest wins, and it matches within floor(letters × maxEditRatio) edits (`Hey Studio` = 9 letters = 2 edits; a 5-letter phrase tolerates 1, so `Hey Al` hears `Hey all`: pick a longer name). MEASURED (#NEW-56, docs/talk-spike.md `Wake word false accepts`): maxEditRatio 0.25 gave 0 false accepts in 8.5 h of mixed corpus audio per language for Hey Triage, Hey Ops, Hey Studio and Hey Assistant; 1/3 would take `He assisted at it` for Hey Assistant and `Hey boss` / `Hey Oma` for Hey Ops, so it stays 0.25 (the `corpus` and `near miss a looser match would take` cases). A phrase without a letter or digit never matches. `rest` = the text after the matched words, leading punctuation and spaces dropped, its first letter capitalised (null = no match). TURN: a match is a push-to-talk key-down for one turn (worker event `woke`, then the same level / partial / heard / empty as a Listen, the capsule ×1): the segment from its padded start seeds the utterance, everything heard is joined as above and loses the phrase (`rest` again; unchanged when the longer transcript no longer opens with it), and the worker ends the turn itself (`turn`): never while a segment is open, after turnEndMs of quiet (since the last segment's padded end) once a command was heard, after noCommandMs while only the phrase was (empty: a false wake costs one capsule and sends nothing), and at maxTurnMs regardless. A push-to-talk key-down replaces a running turn (no answer for it) and borrows the open microphone; the wake word resumes after every turn and Listen. A CALL TAKES PRECEDENCE (`micOwnerCases` at the top level). NO SELF-WAKE (#1263 review): while a reply is being spoken, and for echoTailMs after it ends, every frame the microphone hears counts as the reply's: a segment whose padded start falls among those frames is never checked (no transcription), so the agent's own voice can neither wake it nor barge in on itself; a phrase said after the reply wakes as usual. Wake word off (or Mute) ends a wake turn in flight in the worker, unanswered, and a `woke` that reaches the host after the wake word was taken back is cancelled there (CancelListen), never sent. COOLDOWN (#NEW-86): for cooldownMs after a wake turn ends (answered, empty, replaced or cut at maxTurnMs) the frames the reopened scan hears count as the turn's, exactly like the echo tail: a segment whose padded start falls in the cooldown is never checked (`cooldown`: msSinceTurn = when the segment's padded start was heard, null = no wake turn yet), so a trailing phrase or an echo of the command can't open a second turn at once; a segment that began in the cooldown stays unchecked even when it runs past it, and a phrase said after the cooldown wakes as usual. A push-to-talk Listen has no cooldown.

micOwnerCases._: #NEW-56 + NEW-55 (#1265 review): who owns the voice device's microphone. ONE owner at a time, never two capture streams: `wake` (the wake word's scan), `listen` (a push-to-talk Listen or a wake turn, which borrows the scan's microphone), `call` (a local call, behind its echo canceller) or null (closed; a REMOTE call hears the caller's stream and keeps the device's microphone closed). A CALL TAKES PRECEDENCE: Call closes the wake word's microphone (a wake turn in flight is replaced, unanswered), the wake scan pauses for the WHOLE call (a phrase said into a local call is the call's utterance, `said`, never a `woke`; Wake handed over during a call is kept and waits), and it comes back after Hangup; a push-to-talk Listen during a call is refused at once (`empty`: nothing heard, nothing sent, the call and its reply go on). Steps in order: `do` = wake (the host hands the phrase) | call | remoteCall | hangup | listen (a key-down) | phrase (the person says the wake phrase into the device); `mic` = the owner once the step settled; `answer` = what the step produced: woke | said | empty | null (nothing). Replayed by the speech worker's tests (apps/desktop/crates/voice/src/listener.rs).

echoGate._: #NEW-92 (decision on #NEW-9's thread, 2026-10-27): a LOCAL call (the voice device's own microphone next to its own speakers; DESKTOP ONLY: phones and web capture with the OS echo canceller, so a remote call never passes here) hears the agent's reply through the worker's echo canceller, which needs a few seconds of reply to converge. (1) ONE OUTPUT STREAM PER CALL: the voice device plays every reply of the call on one stream, open from the first reply to Hangup and playing silence in between, and the canceller's reference is what that stream hands the device (silence included), so the echo stays one fixed delay behind its reference and the canceller keeps its converged delay across replies (a player per reply moved it by tens of ms each time and the canceller fell back to ~0 dB). (2) The BARGE-IN GATE, on the canceller's output only (never the raw microphone). Per 32 ms frame: `level` = the frame's level after the canceller (dBFS) and `reference` = the reply's reference ENVELOPE, its loudest 32 ms block over the last echoWindowMs (covers the echo's delay and the room's tail). A reply is AUDIBLE while reference >= replyFloorDb. While nothing is audible every frame at or above `threshold` counts, and bargeInMs of counted frames in the open utterance is the barge-in (voice-call.json `bargeInMs`). Every audible frame adds `level - reference` to the call's history (its last echoFloorFrames); the ECHO FLOOR = the history's median (sorted, the element at index length/2), or initialFloorDb while it holds fewer than echoFloorMinFrames; it tracks how well the canceller removes the echo, so the gate is strict before convergence and again after a divergence. While a reply is audible a frame counts only when it is at or above `threshold` AND, once the floor is at or below convergedFloorDb (CONVERGED), `level - reference` >= echo floor + marginDb (the floor as it stood before this frame); while the floor is above convergedFloorDb (not converged yet, including while it is initialFloorDb) it counts only when `level` >= unconvergedMicDb, an ABSOLUTE microphone level (#1281 review: the reference's dBFS and the microphone's sit on unrelated gains, the output volume and the microphone's, so before the floor measured their relation a margin over the reference means nothing), and the barge-in needs unconvergedBargeInMs of counted frames. A pause that closes the utterance starts the count again. The floor learns from every audible frame, speech or not, EXCEPT a frame that counts within the first echoFloorHoldMs of its utterance (that is the member, who must never raise the bar against themself; after it a canceller that diverged still teaches the floor). An utterance heard while a reply was audible that never became a barge-in is the reply's echo: never transcribed, no partial, never said. `bargeInCases`: `frames` = runs of [probability, level, reference (null = nothing audible), count], followed in the replay by 10 closing frames [0.1, -60, the last run's reference]; `speechStartedAt` = the 0-based frame that emits speechStarted, null = none; `said` = whether the utterance is said. (3) The ECHO TEXT RULE: a finished utterance (and a partial) whose words are the reply's own is dropped, never said nor sent as a turn, UNLESS it barged in over the reply (#1281 review: then it is the member, whatever it repeats; and an utterance heard over the reply that never barged in is never transcribed, so the rule reads what is heard after a reply, within its hold): words = lower case, letters and digits only (`I've` = `ive`); it is the echo when it has at least echoTextMinWords words (a short answer like "merge it" to "Should I merge it or close it?" is the member's) and at least echoTextCoverage of its words appear IN ORDER in one sentence of the call's last two replies (voice.json `speechChunkCases` with streaming true: the reply's sentences) or in two neighbouring ones (a segment can straddle a boundary); a reply's sentences count from its start until spokenHoldMs after it ended. `echoTextCases`.
